raw_case_text: At 12 years of age the patient was admitted with gastroenteritis, generalized intestinal edema and severe nephrotic syndrome progressing to acute renal failure. Quantitative CMV PCR was positive >2 x 106 copies/ml in blood and positive in a renal biopsy (not quantified in tissue). Renal histology showed focal-segmental glomerulosclerosis with extracapillary hypercellularity and mild tubulointerstitial atrophy. Ultrastructural findings showed complete pedicellar effacement characteristic of minimal change nephropathy and no intracellular inclusions or antibody deposits were demonstrated on cytopathology (Figure 1D). Immunofluorescence was faintly positive for C3 and IgG and negative for C1q, IgA, IgM, and fibrin. Exome files were screened for pathogenic podocin mutations that can be associated with nephrotic syndrome, and no pathogenic variants were identified. Interestingly, elevations in CMV titers in blood seemed to precede nephrotic syndrome relapses and correlate with increases in proteinuria (Figure 1F). Due to chronic systemic CMV infection and severe nephrotic syndrome with acute renal failure, she required intermittent critical level care and treatment with systemic steroids. She also received IVIG, broad-spectrum antibiotics, Pneumocystis jiroveci prophylaxis with cotrimoxazole, ganciclovir progressing to foscarnet due to proven resistant CMV strains and hyperimmune CMV-specific immunoglobulin (Cytogam ). Despite aggressive anti-viral therapy, it was impossible to fully control the CMV infection or the nephrotic syndrome that fluctuated in accordance with blood CMV titers that remained between 1 x 106 and 4 x 106 copies/ml despite aggressive treatment. Immunosuppressive therapy, first mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) later cyclosporine were initiated. She had an initial response to this treatment achieving reduction of proteinuria. Unfortunately, CMV infection could not be cleared and the nephrotic syndrome finally became unresponsive to treatment. In this clinical context stem cell transplant was not feasible. During this final end stage disease, she developed Pneumocytis jiroveci pneumonia and fungal lung infection (Figure 1E). Bronchoalveolar lavage was positive for Pneumocystis jiroveci, CMV and galactomannan. She progressed to multi-organ failure and died at 13 years of age, 1 year after her initial admission for nephrotic syndrome associated with systemic CMV infection.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 12-year-old female patient presented with gastroenteritis, generalized intestinal edema, and severe nephrotic syndrome progressing to acute renal failure.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Admitted at 12 years of age with acute gastroenteritis, generalized bowel wall edema, and severe nephrotic syndrome complicated by acute renal failure, the patient experienced a 1-year course of chronic high-level systemic cytomegalovirus (CMV) viremia (1 x 10^6 to 4 x 10^6 copies/mL) where blood CMV viral load spikes directly preceded and correlated with nephrotic syndrome relapses and proteinuria surges, ultimately culminating at age 13 in refractory nephrotic syndrome, opportunistic pulmonary infections, and multiorgan failure.
subjective.past_medical_history: Primary immunodeficiency / chronic systemic CMV susceptibility (negative exome screening for pathogenic podocin mutations).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for gastroenteritis, generalized edema/anasarca, oliguria/acute renal failure, and terminal respiratory failure.

objective.physical_examination: Generalized and intestinal edema with severe nephrotic syndrome and intermittent critical illness.
objective.routine_investigations: Massive nephrotic-range proteinuria and acute renal failure fluctuating in parallel with blood CMV viral loads.
objective.advanced_workup: Quantitative blood CMV PCR was persistently elevated at >2 x 10^6 copies/mL (fluctuating between 1 x 10^6 and 4 x 10^6 copies/mL despite therapy), and renal biopsy tissue was positive for CMV by PCR. Renal biopsy light microscopy demonstrated focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) with extracapillary hypercellularity and mild tubulointerstitial atrophy; immunofluorescence was faintly positive for C3 and IgG (negative C1q, IgA, IgM, fibrin); electron microscopy showed complete foot process (pedicellar) effacement without viral inclusions or immune deposits. Exome sequencing excluded pathogenic podocin mutations. Terminal bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) was positive for Pneumocystis jirovecii, cytomegalovirus (CMV), and Aspergillus galactomannan.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Diagnosed with chronic antiviral-resistant systemic and renal cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection driving relapsing-remitting focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) / severe nephrotic syndrome and acute renal failure (confirmed by blood CMV PCR loads of 1-4 x 10^6 copies/mL, positive renal tissue CMV PCR, and FSGS with complete podocyte foot process effacement on renal biopsy), complicated terminally by Pneumocystis jirovecii, CMV, and galactomannan-positive fungal pneumonia. Treated with intravenous ganciclovir switched to foscarnet for proven ganciclovir-resistant CMV strains, CMV-specific hyperimmune globulin (Cytogam), IVIG, systemic corticosteroids, mycophenolate mofetil, and cyclosporine (stem cell transplantation was unfeasible). Despite transient proteinuria reduction, both CMV viremia and nephrotic syndrome became refractory, and the patient died of multiorgan failure at 13 years of age.
